# A simulation owns its session

[Use C++ member declaration order to release private communication before MPI finalizes.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

A simulation object can own MPI for a standalone executable. Its members
must express the dependency order. This refactors the class-owned MPI
example into a session whose teardown is also observable.

## Declare owners before their dependants

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="session"}
```

C++ constructs members in declaration order and destroys them in reverse
order. The environment is created first, the WORLD wrapper second, and the
duplicated communicator last. Teardown frees the private communicator
before the environment finalizes MPI. Reordering an initializer list would
not change this rule; declaration order is what matters.

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="lifetime" dedent=2}
```

[`MPI_Finalized`](https://www.open-mpi.org/doc/v3.1/man3/MPI_Finalized.3.php)
is one of the MPI queries permitted after finalization. We
use it to verify the end of the session, not to perform more communication.
The rank and rank sum were captured while the communicator was valid.

## Make ownership visible at the call site

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun
```

The empty input is unused. The root CSV includes `finalized=1` after the
session block ends, alongside the independently checkable rank sum. Tests
exercise both one and two ranks. This small object is a standalone runtime
owner; an application embedding OpenPFC after its own `MPI_Init` must borrow
the host runtime instead. See the
[communicator implementation](https://github.com/VTT-ProperTune/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/mpi/communicator.hpp)
for owned duplicate cleanup and the
[host orchestrator](../../coupling/host-orchestrator/index.qmd) for the
corresponding field exchange seam.

The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson.
